subject: Resilience pulse and QBR-ready action compact
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Resilience pulse and QBR-ready action compact

Team —

Quick note to start the QBR prep thread: last Thursday's 30-min degradation in eu-west impacted a small set of enterprise routes (primarily Acme Corp). I pulled a 1-page timeline and an initial action register for runbook and capacity fixes — attached.

Ask: can each of you confirm ownership for the high-priority items below by EOD tomorrow so I can fold into the exec summary slide? I want the QBR deck to have a one-slide incident narrative + 3 concrete mitigations with owners and ETA.

High-priority asks (short):
- Root cause validation: confirm whether the kernel selection misrouted batch jobs or if it was an autoscaler mis-configuration (owner: TBD)
- SLA remediation: temporary routing rule to avoid eu-west failover during peak (owner: TBD)
- Communication: customer-facing timeline and credit recommendation (owner: Hannah)

Attachments: incident_timeline.pdf, action_register.csv

I prefer concise replies (assign / accept / need context). I will compile and circulate the exec slide tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Resilience pulse and QBR-ready action compact

Aditya —

Assigning tentative owners below:
- Root cause validation: Neha (Neha please confirm whether kernel selection is culpable or if telemetry missed an autoscale spike)
- SLA remediation: Vivek (please propose temp routing rule and fallback thresholds)
- Communication and credits: Hannah (I support 10% credit for the impacted window; include legal review)

I'll add a short note on tying the mitigations to OKR KRs (reduce cross-region incident surface).

Laura
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Resilience pulse and QBR-ready action compact

Assigning myself for root cause validation. Quick snapshot from my initial analysis:
- Early telemetry shows a brief spike in concurrent prepended-batch jobs at minute 14 of the event; kernel selection logs show mismatched capability labels for a small subset of gpus.
- I do not yet see autoscaler API throttling; that will need cross-check with control-plane metrics (I will pull).

I've attached a latency_heatmap.png (sample of affected routes) and added two items in action_register.csv:
- RC-1: detailed kernel-selection trace (owner: Neha; ETA 2026-12-06)
- RC-2: control-plane throttle audit (owner: TBD infra; ETA 2026-12-07)

Neha

Thanks for the quick coordination. A couple points from Acme Ops:
- The impacted routes hit our critical inference paths for live recommendations — the window caused a measurable drop in CTR; we need the customer timeline and confirmation of credits.

Date: 2026-12-03T10:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Resilience pulse and QBR-ready action compact

Team + Sarah —

Proposed temporary containment (short):
- Add a routing rule to divert new high-concurrency batch prepends away from eu-west into eu-central for a 48-hour window during the next peak (no changes required on Acme's side; we will do on our control plane).
- Override kernel selection fallback threshold: raise compatibility tolerance by 5% for the window while we validate RC-1.
- I will push these as a canary at 11:00 PST tomorrow and monitor 1-min SLOs.

Action items (updated, from action_register.csv):
- ACT-1: Routing rule (owner: Vivek; ETA: 2026-12-04 11:00 PST)
- ACT-2: Customer timeline + credit recommendation (owner: Hannah; ETA: 2026-12-04 EOD)
- ACT-3: RC trace completion (owner: Neha; ETA: 2026-12-06)

I'll post the canary results to the shared drive link and update the QBR slide once we have the metrics.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Engineering

Subject: Re: Resilience pulse and QBR-ready action compact

Thanks all — consolidating for the exec slide and QBR notes:

Executive summary (one paragraph for the deck):
Last week's brief eu-west degradation affected a targeted set of enterprise routes for one 30-minute window. Initial RCA points to a small kernel-selection mismatch during a short concurrent prepended-batch spike; no evidence of autoscaler API throttling so far. We will implement a short 48-hour routing containment to prevent recurrence during the upcoming peak, complete a kernel-selection trace, and provide Acme Corp a customer timeline plus a credit recommendation.

Owners and ETAs (finalized):
- ACT-1: Routing containment (Vivek) — canary 2026-12-04 11:00 PST
- ACT-2: Customer timeline + credit recommendation (Hannah) — 2026-12-04 EOD
- ACT-3: Kernel-selection trace (Neha) — 2026-12-06
- ACT-4: Control-plane throttle audit (Infra) — 2026-12-07

Next steps: I'll drop the one-slide incident narrative into the QBR deck at the Drive link (see related_links). Laura: can you align the OKR note tying this to "reduce cross-region incident surface"? Vivek: once canary completes, please ping this thread with 1-min SLO snapshots. Hannah: please coordinate legal for the credit language.

Attached: incident_timeline.pdf, action_register.csv

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference
